flashcards.front_question: Differentiate between magnetic and non-magnetic materials with examples.
flashcards.back_answer:
Magnetic materials are strongly attracted by magnets (e.g., Iron, Steel, Nickel, Cobalt). Non-magnetic materials are not attracted (e.g., Wood, Plastic, Glass, Rubber, Copper, Aluminum).

• Concept Pair: Magnetic (Attracted) ↔ Non-magnetic (No attraction).
• Memory Trigger / Icon: 🧲 [Magnet pulling Iron Nails] vs 🪵 [Wood Block]
flashcards.mnemonic_trigger: Memory Key: Connect observation to principle.

flashcards.front_question: Where is the magnetic force concentrated in a bar magnet?
flashcards.back_answer:
At the two extreme ends known as the magnetic poles (North Pole 'N' and South Pole 'S'). Magnetic force is weakest at the exact center.

• Memory Trigger / Icon: 🧲 [Bar Magnet with Clustered Iron Filings at Ends]
• Verification: Rolling a bar magnet in a pile of steel paperclips.
flashcards.mnemonic_trigger: Memory Key: Connect observation to principle.

flashcards.front_question: How can an unmagnetized iron sewing needle be magnetized using the single-touch method?
flashcards.back_answer:
Stroke the needle repeatedly (30–40 times) in one direction along its length using one fixed pole of a bar magnet, lifting the magnet clear between strokes.

• Method: Single-Touch Magnetization.
• Memory Trigger / Icon: 🪡🧲 [Needle stroked in one direction with Magnet]
• Verification: Floating magnetized needle on cork in water acts as compass.
flashcards.mnemonic_trigger: Memory Key: Connect observation to principle.

flashcards.front_question: Why is magnetic repulsion considered the only sure test for confirming if an object is a magnet?
flashcards.back_answer:
A magnet attracts both opposite magnetic poles and unmagnetized magnetic materials (iron). Repulsion occurs exclusively between like poles of two magnets.

• Concept Pair: Attraction (Ambiguous) ↔ Repulsion (Definite Magnetism).
• Memory Trigger / Icon: ↔️ [Two Like Poles N-N Repelling]
• Rule: If an object is pushed away by a magnet pole, it is a magnet.
flashcards.mnemonic_trigger: Memory Key: Connect observation to principle.

flashcards.front_question: What physical actions cause a magnet to lose its magnetic properties (demagnetization)?
flashcards.back_answer:
1. Heating to high temperatures
2. Hammering or hard striking
3. Dropping repeatedly from heights
4. Improper storage without keepers.

• Memory Trigger / Icon: 🔥🔨💥 [Flame, Hammer & Dropping Magnet]
• Prevention: Store bar magnets in pairs with opposite poles separated by wood and soft iron keepers.
flashcards.mnemonic_trigger: Memory Key: Connect observation to principle.

The fundamental property of a freely suspended magnet to always come to rest aligning itself along Earth's geographic North-South direction.

• Phonetic / Usage: Directive (/daɪˈrek.tɪv/) — adjective.
• Memory Trigger / Icon: 🧭 [Magnetic Compass pointing North]
• Application: Maritime navigation across open oceans.
flashcards.mnemonic_trigger: Memory Key: Connect observation to principle.

flashcards.front_question: What was the 'Matsya-yantra' used by ancient Indian navigators?
flashcards.back_answer:
A floating magnetic iron fish suspended in an oil vessel that aligned with North-South directions, serving as an early magnetic compass for ocean voyages.

• Historical Source: Ancient Indian Maritime Navigation Tradition.
• Memory Trigger / Icon: 🐟🧭 [Iron Fish in Water Bowl]
• Significance: Precursor to modern magnetic compasses.
flashcards.mnemonic_trigger: Memory Key: Connect observation to principle.

flashcards.front_question: Why do magnetic poles always exist in inseparable pairs?
flashcards.back_answer:
Magnetism is created by subatomic atomic loop currents. Breaking a bar magnet in half creates two smaller magnets, each possessing a new North and South pole.

• Rule: Isolated magnetic monopoles do NOT exist in nature.
• Memory Trigger / Icon: ✂️🧲 [Broken Magnet forming N-S pairs]
• Result: 1 Magnet → Cut → 2 Complete Magnets.
flashcards.mnemonic_trigger: Memory Key: Connect observation to principle.

flashcards.back_answer:
A naturally occurring dark magnetic mineral (iron oxide) discovered in ancient times that naturally attracts iron pieces.

• Discovery Legend: Magnes the shepherd in Magnesia whose iron-tipped staff stuck to black rock.
• Memory Trigger / Icon: 🪨 [Natural Black Lodestone Ore]
flashcards.mnemonic_trigger: Memory Key: Connect observation to principle.

flashcards.front_question: How does a magnetic compass work?
flashcards.back_answer:
It consists of a light, magnetized needle pivoted freely inside a glass-covered metallic dial marked with cardinal directions (N, S, E, W). The needle aligns with Earth's magnetic field.

• Memory Trigger / Icon: 🧭 [Compass Dial with Red North Needle]
• Usage: Hikers, sailors, and pilots determining direction.
flashcards.mnemonic_trigger: Memory Key: Connect observation to principle.

flashcards.front_question: Name three modern technological devices that utilize magnets.
flashcards.back_answer:
1. Electric motors (in fans, washing machines)
2. Speakers & Headphones (sound vibration)
3. Maglev Trains (frictionless magnetic levitation)
4. MRI Machines (medical body scanning).

• Memory Trigger / Icon: 🚆🔊 [Maglev Train & Speaker Icon]
flashcards.mnemonic_trigger: Memory Key: Connect observation to principle.

flashcards.front_question: State the Law of Magnetic Poles.
flashcards.back_answer:
• Like magnetic poles REPEL each other (N-N repels, S-S repels).
• Unlike magnetic poles ATTRACT each other (N-S attracts).

• Formula/Rule: Like = Repel; Unlike = Attract.
• Memory Trigger / Icon: ➡️⬅️ [N-S Attracting] vs ⬅️➡️ [N-N Repelling]
flashcards.mnemonic_trigger: Memory Key: Connect observation to principle.

flashcards.front_question: How should bar magnets be safely stored when not in use?
flashcards.back_answer:
In pairs with opposite poles (N-S) side-by-side, separated by a wooden strip, with soft iron pieces (keepers) placed across both ends.

• Memory Trigger / Icon: 🪵🧲 [Magnets with Wooden Block & Iron Keepers]
• Purpose: Prevents self-demagnetization over time.
flashcards.mnemonic_trigger: Memory Key: Connect observation to principle.

flashcards.front_question: Describe Activity 4.2: Testing magnetic force through obstacles.
flashcards.back_answer:
Place iron paperclips inside a glass tumbler. Move a strong bar magnet along the outside wall. The clips follow the magnet movement through glass and water.

• Conclusion: Magnetic field forces pass through non-magnetic barriers (glass, water, paper).
• Memory Trigger / Icon: 🍸🧲 [Glass Tumbler with Paperclip following Outer Magnet]
flashcards.mnemonic_trigger: Memory Key: Connect observation to principle.

flashcards.front_question: Why does Earth behave like a giant magnet?
flashcards.back_answer:
Liquid iron and nickel circulating in Earth's molten outer core generate electric currents, creating a planetary magnetic field with magnetic poles near geographic poles.

• Memory Trigger / Icon: 🌍🧲 [Earth with Internal Giant Bar Magnet]
• Effect: Causes compass needles on surface to point North.
flashcards.mnemonic_trigger: Memory Key: Connect observation to principle.
